html:
King of Bamum in the western grasslands of Cameroon from the 1880s until the French deposed him in 1931, known for inventing the Bamum script.

He made the script from the 1890s, refined it into a syllabary, and used it for a history of his people, a book of laws and medicine, and maps. He opened schools, built a large palace at Foumban, and created a new religion blending Islam, Christianity and Bamum belief. He first worked with the Germans of Kamerun, who admired him; the French saw him as a rival and exiled him to Yaounde, where he died. His palace is now a museum.
sum: King of Bamum in the western grasslands of Cameroon from the 1880s until the French deposed him in 1931, known for inventing the Bamum script.
